title: Projects
text:
Project 2
Graduate Research | University of New Hampshire
Investigating dissolved organic nitrogen (DON) contributions to total nitrogen deposition using archived precipitation samples and long-term environmental datasets. The project explores how nitrogen deposition varies over time and its potential influence on watershed biogeochemistry.
Tools: R, Data Analysis, Hindcasting, Watershed Biogeochemistry

title: Projects
text:
Project 3
Graduate Research | University of New Hampshire
Investigating the chemistry of atmospheric deposition and throughfall to better understand how precipitation interacts with forest canopies and influences nutrient cycling in forest ecosystems. This research explores differences in precipitation chemistry, nutrient inputs, and the role of forest canopies in watershed biogeochemical processes.
Tools: R, Data Analysis, Precipitation Chemistry, Throughfall Monitoring, Watershed Biogeochemistry

title: Personal Introduction
text:
Currently I am an aspiring PhD student at the University of New Hampshire. My research interests include watershed biogeochemistry, nutrient cycling, nitrogen deposition, and soil biochemistry. I am particularly interested in understanding how environmental changes influence water quality and forested ecosystems.



M.S. in Environmental and Soil Sciences, University of Tennessee, Knoxville (2025) B.S. in Environmental and Soil Sciences, University of Tennessee, Knoxville (2023), Summa Cum Laude



I previously worked as the Staff Environmental Scientist for the Town of Charlestown, Rhode Island, focusing on water quality and wastewater management.
My academic career covers a wide variety of topics in environmental research, including: GIS and spatial analysis, agricultural fieldwork, laboratory instruction, TA mentorship, and statistical water quaility data analysis. I enjoy combining field observations and computational tools to better understand drivers of environmental processes.
Thanks for checking out my web site!
